title: Giant rogue waves were doubted until a sensor caught one in 1995
body: For centuries sailors described walls of water appearing out of nowhere, and many scientists doubted them, because standard wave models said such giants should be almost impossibly rare. On 1 January 1995, instruments on the Draupner gas platform in the North Sea recorded a wave 25.6 m high, while the waves around it were about 12 m. It was the first rogue wave ever measured by an instrument, and it pushed oceanographers to rethink how waves combine.

slides.question: How tall was the rogue wave recorded at the Draupner platform?
slides.explanation: 25.6 m, while the waves around it were about 12 m. Measured on 1 January 1995 in the North Sea, it was the first rogue wave ever caught by an instrument.

slides.heading: Wave heights at the Draupner platform, 1 January 1995
slides.note: Wave height is trough to crest; ‘typical’ is the significant wave height at the time.

slides.clue: The North Sea gas platform whose instruments recorded the wave on New Year’s Day 1995
slides.detail: The platform stands about 160 km south-west of the southern tip of Norway. Its wave sensor caught the 25.6 m wave.
